The guard requires maxClientHelloLength != 0, and most default paths pass 0: AbstractSniHandler() calls this(0, 0L), SniHandler(Mapping) -> SniHandler(AsyncMapping) -> this(mapping, 0, 0L), and the handshake-timeout-only constructors delegate with 0 as well. The mitigation therefore only takes effect when the application explicitly passes a maxClientHelloLength in [1, 0xFFFFFF].

severity.derivation_method: CVSS 3.1 base metrics were chosen by the collector from the verified code path and the advisory text, then the base score was computed with the official 3.1 formula: AV:N (a remote client receives the upstream's response), AC:H (the upstream must be malicious or compromised and must answer the upgrade), PR:N, UI:R (the client must open the WebSocket upgrade), S:U, C:N (the leaked headers give no direct read of protected data), I:L (injected hop-by-hop headers can alter client/proxy connection state), A:N. The independent reviewer must recompute this vector and may replace or reject it; if the reviewer rejects it, the dossier must not be promoted.
severity.discrepancy_note: Severity is the only field in this dossier that is not a published value. Every published CVSS slot is null; the advisory provides only the label 'low'. The score is a documented analyst reading, flagged so that it can be audited and replaced.

metric_rationale.A: N - the repro shows no availability impact.
metric_rationale.AC: H - exploitation presupposes a malicious or compromised upstream that sets the headers; the client cannot inject them through Caddy.
metric_rationale.AV: N - the 101 response is delivered over the network to any client that opens the proxied WebSocket route.
metric_rationale.C: N - the repro shows header leakage only; no protected data is read.
metric_rationale.I: L - Alt-Svc/Set-Cookie/Proxy-Authenticate injection can change client connection state, but no integrity compromise was demonstrated beyond that.
metric_rationale.PR: N - no privileges on Caddy or the upstream are required of the victim.
metric_rationale.S: U - the impact stays within the client/proxy connection.
metric_rationale.UI: R - the victim has to establish the upgraded connection for the leaked response headers to reach it.

severity.numeric_level_rationale: The derived base score is 3.1, which is Low (0.1-3.9) and agrees with the advisory's published qualitative label 'low'. Because no published numeric metric exists, this score must not be cited as a vendor or CNA score.

additional_verified_affected.evidence: The identical imports-key code injection reproduces on the 3.10.1 tag blob: lodash.js line 10727 assigns options.imports with assignWith(baseAssign({}, ...)) and line 10810 passes the keys to Function(importsKeys, ...), with no reForbiddenIdentifierChars check anywhere in 3.x. comma-pad and undefined-value payloads both set the marker. CVE-2021-23337's own OSV range starts at introduced 0, consistent with 3.x being affected.

range_completeness.policy: The dataset retains the authoritative published range in affected_range and does not rewrite it; the demonstrated wider exposure is recorded here, in discrepancies and in limitations, per the Django CVE-2020-7471 precedent (data_quality_findings.md item 23). No claim is made that 3.10.1 is the lowest affected version.

category_l2: Code injection through template compilation: `_.template` merges the caller-supplied `options.imports` with `assignInWith` (so inherited enumerable keys are copied), never validates the merged key names, and passes them as parameter names to `Function(importsKeys, ...)`. Key names containing commas, parentheses, braces, brackets, slashes or whitespace break out of the parameter list and execute at template call time. Only the separate `variable` option was validated, a gap left by the CVE-2021-23337 fix.
discrepancies: Patched-version disagreement: CVE.org and the GitHub advisory say 4.18.1; OSV and NVD's CPE range say 4.18.0. Source inspection shows the validation already present in 4.18.0. The dossier records 4.18.1 and states the 4.18.0 caveat.

The advisory's only fix reference, 3469357c (2021-02-17), is the CVE-2021-23337 `variable`-option fix and is an ancestor of 4.17.21, 4.17.23, 4.18.0 and 4.18.1. A check that treats any referenced fix commit as an ancestor as 'not affected' would wrongly clear this snapshot. The real fix, 879aaa93, is identified by its message (it names both this CVE and the GHSA), its diff, and its ancestry: absent at 4.17.23, present at 4.18.0/4.18.1.
Severity disagreement: NVD primary 9.8 CRITICAL (AC:L) versus CNA/GitHub/OSV 8.1 HIGH (AC:H). Same impact metrics, different attack complexity.

lodash 4.17.22 was never published to npm (registry time and versions jump 4.17.21 to 4.17.23), yet every advisory range includes it. Ranges over this ecosystem must not be read as 'every version in between exists'.

The published npm tarball of 4.17.23 ships a lodash.js (sha256 71b4b7f5) that differs from the git tag blob (sha256 2dc5f1b8) yet contains the same vulnerable construct at the same lines and reproduces. The snapshot is the git tag; the npm build is independent corroboration, not the snapshot content.

The plain release tag 4.17.23 and the channel tag 4.17.23-npm are different commits (dec55b7a, 159 files vs 835a537f, 1054 built files). The evaluation target is the plain source tag; the channel tag was considered and rejected as a distribution artifact (see the abandoned 4.17.22-npm recon).

npm marks lodash@4.18.0 deprecated with the message 'Bad release. Please use lodash@4.17.21 instead.' (lodash-es, lodash-amd and lodash.template 4.18.0 are likewise deprecated). That explains why CVE.org and the GitHub advisory recommend 4.18.1 while OSV and NVD's CPE boundary stop at 4.18.0. The reason for the deprecation is not documented in the repository history; only the npm deprecation string is public evidence.

The published lower bound >=4.0.0 is incomplete: the same imports-key injection reproduces on lodash 3.10.1, which has the assignWith/Function sink at 10727/10810 and no reForbiddenIdentifierChars check (see affected_packages[0].range_completeness). The upper bound is unaffected. The dataset keeps the authoritative published range instead of inventing a wider one, and does not claim to know the lowest affected version.

The absence of 4.17.22 is specific to the lodash package: lodash-es published 4.17.22 on 2025-12-16 and lodash-amd on 2025-12-17, and the repository carries 4.17.22-amd/-es/-npm channel tags, but there is no plain 4.17.22 tag. Every advisory range includes a version that does not exist for the package this snapshot tracks.

At 4.18.1 the inherited-key variant does not throw: the fix also replaced assignInWith with assignWith, so an imports key inherited through the prototype is dropped before validation. Only own-key variants raise 'Invalid `imports` option passed into `_.template`'. Nothing executes in either case, so the fix is complete for both shapes.

The published npm tarball's package/package.json has no `private` field (npm strips it) while the git tag's package.json sets private: true. Artifact metadata is not byte-identical to the tag; the tarball's lodash.js differs from the tag blob only in two jsdoc comment lines (20-line unified diff, no code change).

GitHub publishes two different first-patched versions for the same advisory: the rendered repository advisory page says 4.18.1 (quoted in range_expressions), while the GitHub Advisory Database JSON read through the API during the independent selection review of 2026-10-22 says 4.18.0. This is a GitHub-internal inconsistency, not a transcription error, and it does not affect the snapshot's affected status.

Publication timestamps differ by surface: the rendered repository advisory page says 2026-03-31T19:03:35Z (recorded in published_at), CVE.org says 2026-03-31T19:25:55.987Z (recorded in published_at_cve_org), and OSV says 2026-04-01T23:51:12Z. All three are kept; none is a substitute for another.

The Debian range describes Debian's patched source package (0.6.3-1 carries a backport of PR 807); it is a downstream range, not evidence that vanilla 0.6.3 is fixed. additional_verified_affected.evidence: Vanilla upstream yaml-cpp-0.6.3 (9a36242) still segfaults on the same input: poc '[ ' x15000 with rc 139 (poc_reproduction.txt). The fix 4edff1f is not an ancestor of 0.6.3 (ancestry.txt). Debian's 0.6.3-1 is fixed only because it backports PR 807.

range_completeness.policy: The dataset keeps the published range and does not widen it. The demonstrated fact that vanilla 0.6.3 is also affected, while Debian 0.6.3-1 is patched, is recorded here and in discrepancies so that no downstream fixed_version is mistaken for an upstream one.

category_l2: Uncontrolled recursion in the single-document YAML parser: SingleDocParser::HandleFlowSequence consumes a '[' token, calls HandleNode, and HandleNode dispatches back into HandleFlowSequence for the next '['. There is no depth counter anywhere in the parser at 0.6.2, so a document of n opening brackets creates O(n) nested C++ stack frames and the process crashes with SIGSEGV before any syntax error is reported. The same cycle exists for flow maps ('{'), compact maps and the scanner's token queue; the 0.7.0 fix bounds it with a DepthGuard at HandleNode.
discrepancies: Fixed-version disagreement between ecosystems: Debian's tracker and OSV record say fixed_version 0.6.3-1, while upstream vanilla 0.6.3 still crashes and the fix commit 4edff1f is not an ancestor of 0.6.3. Debian 0.6.3-1 is a patched package that backports PR 807 (its changelog names CVE-2019-6285 and the patch says it 'cherry-picks the (so-far-unmerged) upstream pull request'). The first upstream release containing the fix is 0.7.0, and that is what the dossier records as the fixed release.

Two sibling CVEs (CVE-2018-20573 Scanner::EnsureTokensInQueue, CVE-2018-20574 HandleFlowMap) are labelled CWE-119 by NVD while CVE-2019-6285 and CVE-2019-6292 are labelled CWE-674. All four are the same stack-exhaustion defect fixed by the same commit; CWE-119 is a misclassification of uncontrolled recursion as a buffer issue.

The CVE.org CNA container ships a placeholder affected object: vendor, product and version are all 'n/a' and problemTypes is 'n/a', so the record itself states no version, CVSS or CWE. Its only reference is issue 660; the CVE Program ADP container adds a 2024 seclists fulldisclosure post. The exact 0.6.2 range comes from NVD's CPE and OSV's GIT range, not from the CVE record itself.

The affected range is not exhaustive: vanilla 0.6.3 is also affected although the published Debian range ends at 0.6.3-1, and older releases with the same parser (0.6.0, 0.6.1, and 0.5.x for the 2017 CVE) were not bisected. The published range and CPE name only 0.6.2.

The fix merged upstream with DepthGuard<2000> but the 0.7.0 release carries DepthGuard<500>, lowered by commit c2793a3 (2020-07-23, 'Fix runtime exceptions in Visual Studio environment. (#926)'). The recorded fixed release therefore rejects nesting at depth 500, not 2000.

CVE-2019-6292 is not covered by a named regression test in the fix commit, although it shares the same root cause and issue family (issue 657 lists HandleCompactMap, HandleMap, HandleFlowSequence, HandleSequence and HandleNode). The fix is family-wide because every path goes through HandleNode.
Publication timestamps differ by surface: CVE.org says 2019-01-14T22:00:00Z, NVD and OSV say 2019-01-14T22:29:00.390Z. Both are kept; neither replaces the other.

GHSA-hg7f-3vww-rc69 publishes the CVE as an identifier, but that advisory is not mirrored into OSV (api.osv.dev returns 404 for the GHSA id), so OSV's alias list for CVE-2019-6285 is empty. The GHSA edge is recorded from the GitHub advisory API instead. No source publishes an upstream semver range: only NVD's CPE, OSV's GIT range and Debian's downstream ECOSYSTEM range name versions.
NVD status is Modified, not final, and the record was last modified 2026-06-17; the score and CPE may still change.

category_l2: Uncaught error in the microservice server: ServerTCP#handleMessage and ServerRMQ#handleMessage convert a client-controlled non-string message pattern with JSON.stringify to derive the handler lookup key. JSON.parse accepts nesting that JSON.stringify cannot re-serialise, so a deeply nested pattern parses on arrival and then throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded. The listener's promise is not caught, the RangeError becomes an unhandled rejection, and Node.js exits under its default --unhandled-rejections=throw. The fix guards the stringification with getPatternAsString and routes handleMessage rejections to handleError.
discrepancies: The fix references do not agree with release containment. GHSA, OSV, NVD and CVE.org all name aa97b514 (the PR head) as a fix commit, but that commit is an ancestor of no tag; the PR was squash-merged as e93c8e12b (in v12.0.2+) and the 11.x line received the dedicated backport e9dcd4c7 (in v11.2.4+). The dossier records all three with their measured ancestry so no reader mistakes aa97b514 for the release-bearing fix.

The publication timestamps differ by surface: CVE.org and OSV say 2026-09-28T21:21:25Z, NVD says 2026-09-28T22:17:32Z, and the GHSA API says 2026-09-29T23:54:44Z. The catalog candidate record says 2026-09-15T08:38:29Z, which is earlier than every advisory surface; the row uses NVD's timestamp and keeps the others here.

NVD's status is 'Awaiting Analysis', not 'Analyzed'. Its only CVSS metric is the GitHub CNA Secondary 3.1 7.5; there is no NVD primary metric and no NVD CPE configuration. The CPE-style range comes from NVD's 'affected' block, which is the CNA's data, not an NVD analysis.

The GHSA says the patched versions are 12.0.2 and 11.2.4 but recommends upgrading to 12.0.3 / 11.2.5. Both 11.2.4 and 12.0.2 are inside the range of the separate advisory GHSA-96h4-vgxj-gvm2, fixed in 11.2.5 / 12.0.3. The row keeps 11.2.4 and 12.0.2 as this CVE's fixed releases because those are the first releases containing this fix.

Two CWEs are assigned. CWE-248 (Uncaught Exception) names the mechanism that terminates the process; CWE-674 (Uncontrolled Recursion) names the stringify recursion. Both are recorded; neither replaces the other.

OSV's GIT range places the 11.x fix at the v11.2.4 tag commit d5046225 and the 12.x fix at the v12.0.2 tag commit ee168a56, while the advisory-level fixed commits are the code commits e9dcd4c7 / e93c8e12b. The tag commits are release commits that contain the code fixes; the ancestry checks were run for both the code commits and the tags.

The microservices package version and the monorepo root version differ: at v11.2.3 packages/microservices/package.json is 11.2.3 while the root package.json is 11.1.26. The affected package is the npm package, not the root monorepo version.

Only the TCP and RabbitMQ transports are affected. The collector reproduced the TCP path only; the RMQ path is asserted from the identical unguarded call at server-rmq.ts 300-302 and the backport diff, not from a broker run. Other transports take the pattern as a string from the broker and never stringify a client object.

category_l2: XMLUtil::GetCharacterRef accumulates a numeric character reference in 32-bit counters guarded only by TIXMLASSERT. A reference such as &#4294967295; overflows the multiplier, so a build with TIXMLASSERT enabled aborts (SIGABRT) instead of rejecting the input; 10.1.0 bounds the value at U+10FFFF and returns 0.

category_l2: actix-http's HTTP/1.1 request parser accepts a request that carries both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding: chunked, then frames the body by chunked. A front-end that frames by Content-Length can therefore be desynchronised, leaving a second request (e.g. GET /admin) in the reused connection. 3.12.1 rejects the ambiguous framing with ParseError::Header.
